title: How to Carry Out Work
note: He defines this as the way a minister with such firmness carries out the work.

couplets.plain: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision. For that decision to sit in delay is wrong.
couplets.pm: Deliberation ends when you reach the firm view that this can’t fail, so go on deliberating until then. If work so decided then lingers, that is a fault. To delay is not to act at the time for action. The moment passes and enemies learn of it and destroy it, so it isn’t finished.

links.quote: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision

couplets.plain: Take your time over what should be done slowly. Don’t delay over what must be done without delay.
couplets.pm: Delay in the kinds of work that are done slowly, and don’t delay in the kinds that aren’t. Which is which can be known from strength and time. Do them the wrong way round and they won’t succeed. He said earlier not to delay, and here he divides that rule in two.

links.quote: Take your time over what should be done slowly
Don’t delay over what must be done without delay
links.reason: Tells someone who keeps delaying that some work must be done without delay.

couplets.plain: Action is good wherever it is possible. Where it isn’t, look for the way that will work and do that.
couplets.pm: Wherever possible, it is good to do the work by war. It is possible when you are stronger than your enemy, and force is best then, because force is what they fear. Where it isn’t possible, when you are equal or weaker, look among conciliation, division and gifts for the means that will succeed.
couplets.note: The words say only “work”. He reads வினை here as war, and the other way as the three other means of statecraft.

links.quote: look for the way that will work
links.reason: Allows direct action where it can be done, and whatever way will work where it can’t.

couplets.plain: Think about it: what is left of a task or an enemy burns you as what is left of a fire does.
couplets.pm: What remains of work begun, and of an enemy you began to root out, will grow and destroy you, as what remains of a fire does. So don’t scorn it and ask what this remnant can do, but finish it. They grow back alike, so he names the enemy too. This is how the strong should work.

links.quote: what is left of a task or an enemy
what is left of a fire

couplets.plain: Wealth, means, time, the work and the place: weigh all five until the darkness clears, then act.
couplets.pm: Weigh these five without confusion and then act: the wealth to be spent and gained, your forces and the enemy’s, the time that suits you and the time that suits them, the work you do well and the work they do well, the place where you win and the place where they win. Weigh them without error, so that you win.

links.quote: weigh all five until the darkness clears

links.reason: Wealth comes first on the list of five.
Time is the third thing to weigh.

couplets.plain: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain you will reach when it is done, and then act.
couplets.pm: Weigh the effort it takes to finish, the obstacles that will come, and the great gain you will reach once they are cleared and the work is done, and then act. Do it if the gain is larger than the effort and the obstacles.

links.quote: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain
links.reason: Sets out what to reckon first: the finish, the obstacles and the gain.

links.quote: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain you will reach

couplets.plain: The way to do a task is this: take in the mind of someone who knows that task from the inside.
couplets.pm: Someone who has begun such work should proceed like this: learn the thinking of one who knows its inner workings. That means someone who has done it before, and his thinking is the means he used. Knowing that, you can use it too and gain the result.

links.quote: someone who knows that task from the inside
links.reason: Makes learning the mind of one who knows the task from inside the way to do it.

couplets.plain: To get one task done by means of another is to bind a wet-cheeked elephant with another elephant.
couplets.pm: Use the work you are doing to finish another like it. That is like using an elephant with cheeks wet with must to bind another such elephant. The wet cheeks show how hard the binding is. Plan so that each task begun becomes the means of finishing another, and all work is easily done.

links.quote: To get one task done by means of another
bind a wet-cheeked elephant with another elephant
links.reason: One wet-cheeked elephant used to bind another models work that wins more work.

couplets.plain: Be quicker to win over those not with you than to do good to your friends.
couplets.pm: For one at work, making friends of those opposed to his enemy is to be done even faster than doing good to his own friends. Both help the work, and both should be done before the enemy sees his weakness. It may also mean keeping his own opponents from joining others.
couplets.note: The plain reading takes ஒட்டார் as those not with you. He takes them first as those not with your enemy, and allows your own opponents as a second reading.

links.quote: win over those not with you
links.reason: Ranks winning over those not with you as more urgent even than doing good to a friend.

couplets.plain: Those who hold little, fearing the trembling within, will bow to the great and take the terms, if they can get them.
couplets.pm: Ministers with little land and fort, facing someone stronger, fear their own side will tremble. If peace can be had, they bow and accept it. The strong rarely agree to it, so he says “if”. If their side flees in fear they are lost, root and all, so give a little and take peace. The proud don’t wish to bow, so he states this as the way of the world.
couplets.sensitive: Tells the weak to submit to the strong.

links.reason: Urges those who hold little to own their weakness and bow to the great for terms.

ideaLinks.quote: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision
